nodes.description:
Goal: finish the stale-graph weak spot of #52, then close every open v0.2 issue and release v0.2.0.
Instructions: user speaks Spanish; PRs need user merge; tags/pushes only after confirmation; #35 to be done together with #55; #18 and #35 moved to v0.3; close #40 with a README section; close #59 without committing kg's own graph.
Discoveries: hybrid/cards reading stale-reported files lifts stale score 0.50-0.65 -> 0.83 but costs 3-4x the context of code; bench called bare kg, failing in subagents without venv; kg's graph.json is 1.17 MB (78 KB compressed) and diffs ~6 lines per code line, so committing it means merge conflicts per PR; Repo ID comes from the clone folder name, so kg add of a published agent layer fails in a differently named folder; __version__ was still 0.1.0.dev0.
Accomplished: PRs #57, #58, #61, #62, #63, #64 merged; issues #59, #60 opened (#59 closed, #60 open); #18, #40 closed; #35 and #18 moved to v0.3 with cross comments on #35/#55; #41 rewritten (static landing, Streamlit parked) and moved to v0.3; tags v0.1.0 (8b9d7b2) and v0.2.0 (05cef90) pushed; GitHub Release v0.2.0 published with tag-pinned absolute links; v0.2 milestone closed (15/15).
Next steps: review the v0.3 table in docs/roadmap.md, then #52 step 3 (scrapy, the decisive test), then rest of #52 (document sections, quoted claims, search limited to changed files); #60 drift; #41 landing; #35+#55 together; optional issue for Repo ID from git remote.
Relevant files: bench/tools.py, docs/benchmark.md, .pre-commit-hooks.yaml, docs/store.md, src/kg/cli.py, src/kg/schema/validation.py, docs/schema.md, README.md, docs/requirements.md, docs/roadmap.md, src/kg/__init__.py

Stale-reads benchmark results
Stale reads: hybrid and cards reach 0.83 on stale questions, at 3-4x the context of code
nodes.description:
What: re-ran the 6 stale questions with hybrid and cards able to read files kg status / stale_graph report; hybrid 0.65->0.83, cards 0.50->0.83; context mean 58,676 (hybrid) and 50,750 (cards) vs code 8,460; tokens 39,174/36,912 vs 33,095.
Why: the stale graph was the weak spot: it warned correctly but the agent could not open files no node cites (e.g. added after the graph).
Where: bench/results/20261015T200647Z-subagent-stale-reads.jsonl, docs/benchmark.md, bench/tools.py (Citations.add_from)
Learned: every answer was right; the two failures ran out of the 25 calls (recorded as max_turns, not re-run to avoid bias); cost comes from reading changed files one by one where code uses one search; next fix is a search limited to changed files; in two runs the agent grep-filtered its own output, which grants no new file; one run per question.

nodes.label: The benchmark runs kg as sys.executable -m kg, never a bare kg
nodes.description:
What: bench run_kg calls the current interpreter with -m kg.
Why: subagents run env/bin/python without activating the venv, so a bare kg is not on PATH and every call failed with FileNotFoundError.
Where: bench/tools.py
Learned: the first batch of 12 stale subagents failed for this and was discarded and re-run in a new session (20261015T200647Z).

nodes.label: Benchmark runs that exhaust the call limit count as failures and are not repeated
nodes.description:
What: a subagent that runs out of its 25 calls is recorded as max_turns with score 0, even if it had found the answer.
Why: repeating until it succeeds would bias the comparison; reading whole files legitimately costs calls.
Where: bench results, docs/benchmark.md
Learned: applied to kgs-tests-update.cards (read 12 changed test files one by one) and kgs-impact-validation.hybrid.

nodes.label: Add a search limited to the files a stale graph reports as changed

Why: stale reads now answer correctly but cost 3-4x the context of the code strategy; this would make uncovered files cost the same as code.
Where: bench/tools.py, part of #52
Learned: proposed in PR #58; not started.

nodes.label: Keep the graph fresh with kg status --check and pre-commit hooks, not a kg hook command or a committing bot
nodes.description:
What: kg status --check exits 1 on modified/added/deleted files (output unchanged); .pre-commit-hooks.yaml publishes kg-extract (re-extracts, fails the commit like a formatter if graph.json changes) and kg-status (check only); docs/store.md 'Keeping the graph fresh' gives a GitHub Actions template with --check.
Why: the stale benchmark shows a stale graph is safe but costly; the parser layer is deterministic and takes seconds, so it can be automated; the agent layer cannot (no LLM in kg, RF-24) and is reviewed instead; the pre-commit framework already handles install/uninstall/stash, so no kg hook command; a workflow that commits the graph adds history noise, loops with other workflows and needs write permissions.
Where: src/kg/cli.py, .pre-commit-hooks.yaml, docs/store.md, README, agent guide + skill; RF-73 moved up to v0.3
Learned: unknown files (unparseable) do not fail --check, else CI fails forever; a no-op kg extract does not rewrite graph.json; tried with pre-commit try-repo on a demo repo; test reads entry: lines by regex to avoid adding PyYAML; incremental extraction (RF-78) not needed.

nodes.label: kg does not commit its own .kg/ graph or run the CI freshness check on itself
nodes.description:
What: #59 closed without dogfooding the CI template; the pre-commit try-repo trial replaces that criterion.
Why: measured on main: graph.json 1.17 MB, 47,000 lines, 78 KB compressed; a merge with 166 code lines gives a 991-line graph diff (line ranges shift, ~6 graph lines per code line), docs-only 0; rebuild with extract + kg add examples/agent/kg.json takes ~2 s. Size is fine, but parallel PRs touching code would conflict on graph.json almost every time; every contributor has kg and rebuilds in 2 s.
Where: issue #59 closing comment
Learned: committing a graph pays off when building it is expensive or readers lack kg; revisit when the MCP server (RF-23) lands and agents on kg should query its graph without building it.

nodes.label: Issue #60: measure graph drift: share of graph at risk in kg status, and accuracy vs graph age
nodes.description:
What: (1) kg status (text and --json) reports share of nodes/edges whose source file changed, split by provenance method, listing agent-layer elements at risk; (2) benchmark curve: code fixed, graphs built at N-1, N-5, N-10, N-20 commits via graph_commit in bench/repos.json, run graph/cards/hybrid, plot score and context vs age, check whether metric (1) predicts the fall to get a re-extract threshold.
Why: kg status says whether the graph is stale but not how much it matters; the user asked how accuracy degrades with commits.
Where: src/kg/update.py, bench/repos.json, docs/benchmark.md; milestone v0.3
Learned: the metric is an indicator of trust, not accuracy; the kg repo itself is the natural subject (kg-stale is one point today); complements #59.

nodes.label: Custom types reported once: warning naming a standard type if similar, otherwise a new 'note' severity
nodes.description:
What: one issue per custom type with all occurrences in a new paths key; a warning names the standard type by near-identical name or a small deterministic synonym table (Tutorial->Document, invokes->calls, links_to->documents, satisfies->implements); anything else is a note, listed on one line in text and in notes in --json (validate, add, extract).
Why: custom types are valid by design (RF-02) but every use looked like an error.
Where: src/kg/schema/validation.py, src/kg/cli.py, docs/schema.md, agent guide + skill
Learned: JSON break: custom types without equivalent move from warnings to notes; DESIGN_DECISION fails the type-name pattern so it is a schema error, not a custom type.

nodes.description:

Criterion 4 in requirements (changelog 1.2) and roadmap point to it and docs/examples.
Why: the user felt a demo was redundant: install is checked by CI and docs/examples/README.md already rebuilds each example; the only gap was showing the graph answering a question.
Where: README.md, docs/requirements.md, docs/roadmap.md
Learned: outputs match benchmark references pca-impact-user and pca-untested; no LLM or clone of kg needed; user approved the requirement change.

nodes.label: Repo node ID comes from the clone folder name, so a published agent layer fails in another folder
nodes.description:
What: kg add rejects an agent layer referencing repo:python-clean-architecture if the repo was cloned under a different folder name.
Why: found while testing Ask the graph from scratch.
Where: src/kg/extract (Repo ID), README Ask the graph ('keep the folder name')
Learned: worked around with a README comment; fragile; proposed a v0.3 issue to derive the ID from the git remote when present (not opened, awaiting user).
